hero.title: Know the state of your insulin.

problem.title: A summer car trip shouldn't be a doubt.
problem.text: A pen in use lasts up to 28 days outside the fridge, but it doesn't like heat. And spoiled insulin can't be seen.

items.title: Current solutions are bulky
items.text: Cooler bags and ice packs take up space in your backpack and, when the ice melts, soak everything around.

items.title: A thermometer only tells you now
items.text: It won't tell you if the pen spent two hours at 35 °C inside the car while you were at the beach.

items.title: When in doubt, throw it out
items.text: Not knowing if it's still good, you either bin the pen as a precaution or take the risk. Both options are bad.

tabs.label: Protects
tabs.title: Double wall, not a drop of ice.
tabs.text: The insulation slows down heat peaks on long trips, so the pen stays at usage temperature without ice packs or bulky bags.

tabs.label: Alerts
tabs.title: Green, amber, red. That's it.
tabs.text: A light ring on the cap shows the status instantly, even with the bottle in a half-open bag or in sunlight.

tabs.label: Remembers
tabs.title: It knows what happened while you were away.
tabs.text: The screen keeps the trip's temperature history and counts the days since the pen was opened. The algorithm estimates the cumulative effect of heat, not just the current value.

items.question: Is this for unopened insulin?
items.answer: No. It is designed for pens already in use (up to 28 days outside the fridge). Unopened insulin should still be kept in the fridge, as the manufacturer states.

items.question: Do I need ice or to charge batteries?
items.answer: It uses no ice: the insulation is dry and double-walled. The cap has low-power electronics for the LED, the screen and the temperature log.

items.question: How much does it cost and when does it arrive?
items.answer: We are still validating the product, so there is no fixed price or date. Those who pre-reserve are told first, with no obligation to buy.

items.question: Is pre-reserving a purchase?
items.answer: No. It is an email expressing interest. We do not ask for payment or bank details.

items.question: Does it replace medical advice?
items.answer: No. It gives you information about the temperature the pen was exposed to. Always follow the insulin manufacturer's and your healthcare team's instructions.

final.title: Join the first-batch list.
final.text: Tell us how you travel and how you carry your insulin today. It helps us build the right product and you'll be among the first to know when it's ready.
